items.reference_answer: The Pollanwser.org app is a full‑stack polling web application developed to strengthen practical development skills. It was built with React.js for the frontend, styled with Tailwind CSS for a responsive UI, and Java Spring Boot for the backend, exposing RESTful APIs. The app features secure user authentication using JWT (JSON Web Token), allowing users to log in and register safely. It supports full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations for both polls and user accounts, and implements token‑based access control throughout the system. The project was created in Bangkok, Thailand, and was showcased on 14 October 2023. A thumbnail image of the project can be viewed at https://res.cloudinary.com/dwnwhonj6/image/upload/v1748333201/portfolio_thumbnails/thumbnail_1748333198700.png.

Held on 8 January 2025 at RMUTT in Thailand, the workshop brought together international students to tackle real‑world environmental problems using Design Thinking and Engineering Design. items.reference_answer: The Vending Machine GUI Application is a graphical simulator created in Python using the PySimpleGUI library. It lets users browse a list of products with images, add items to a virtual basket, adjust quantities, and proceed through a simulated checkout that includes cash insertion, change calculation in Thai Baht, and purchase logging to both text and CSV files. The interface dynamically resizes product images, updates the date/time and basket totals in real time, and provides multi‑window navigation between product selection, basket, payment, and success screens, along with clear user feedback at each step. The project was developed at RMUTT on May 3 2025 and its source code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/Automatic28m/python_vending_machine_2024.

items.reference_answer: Phanlop's portfolio website is a dynamic, interactive platform that showcases his skills, projects, achievements, internships, academic activities, and education. It features a modern, responsive design with animated home‑page introductions (typewriter effects, fade‑ins), sections for each content area, and dynamic content loading via API. The portfolio detail pages display titles, contents, event location (Bangkok, Thailand), event date (May 30 2025), thumbnails, skill tags with custom colors, and a lightbox gallery. Users can log in with JWT‑based authentication. The backend provides a dashboard for managing portfolio entries, including creating, editing, and deleting entries, uploading thumbnails and gallery images, and managing skill types with color selection. Technical highlights include React for the frontend, Node.js/Express.js for the API, responsive design, toast notifications, and secure JWT authentication. The entry was created on May 31 2025, and its thumbnail is available at https://res.cloudinary.com/dwnwhonj6/image/upload/v1748679493/portfolio_thumbnails/thumbnail_1748679492347.jpg.

items.reference_answer: The React Online Shopping App is a React‑based shopping‑cart application created to practice and demonstrate Redux for state management. Developed in Bangkok, Thailand, it was completed on June 2 2025 (the event took place on June 1 2025). The app uses a productReducer to manage cart items and total price, and it supports adding items to the cart, removing items by ID, decreasing item quantity, clearing the entire cart, and dynamically updating the total price. The project showcases Redux actions, reducers, and immutable state updates, providing hands‑on experience with Redux concepts in a React environment. items.reference_answer: The Global Capstone Design Project 2025 (Workshop 2) was a short‑term exchange program jointly organized by Yeungnam University in South Korea and Rajamangala University of Technology Thanyaburi in Thailand. Held on August 4, 2025 in Gyeongju, South Korea, the workshop brought together international students to tackle real‑world environmental problems using Design Thinking and Engineering Design methods. Participants brainstormed and created a Smart Bin System that can recognize and sort trash (plastic, metal, organic, etc.) with sensors and AI classification. They developed a practical, usable, feasible, and sustainable prototype, built a Next.js dashboard linked to a MySQL database to show real‑time classified‑waste data, and enhanced their teamwork, cross‑cultural communication, and early‑stage product design skills.

items.reference_answer: I was selected to represent my university in the ICPC International Collegiate Programming Contest held at KMUTL on September 9, 2025, competing against teams from 26 institutions nationwide. My primary responsibility was to translate all English problem statements into Thai in real time, ensuring my teammates fully understood each challenge. Competing against 69 teams from 38 universities nationwide, I was responsible for developing a drone‑detection system that could detect drones in real time, identify their coordinates and altitude, and track them, sending the data to a dashboard. Our team earned the Top Score for Presentation and the Top Score for Battlefield Integration, marking a significant accomplishment.

items.question: What is the Air Monitor Pro IoT Mini project and what does it include?

variants.verbatim: What is the Air Monitor Pro IoT Mini project and what does it include?
variants.partial: What Air Monitor Pro IoT Mini
variants.natural: the Air Monitor Pro IoT Mini project and what does it include thanks?

items.reference_answer: Air Monitor Pro is a smart industrial environmental guard that provides real‑time monitoring of air quality, safety thresholds, and early fire detection in warehouses, labs, and other industrial spaces. The system combines a rugged, wall‑mountable ESP32‑based hardware enclosure with a cloud‑based Next.js dashboard. It senses PM2.5 dust, CO₂/Smoke gases, temperature and humidity (4‑in‑1), logs alerts in MongoDB, and sends notifications via MQTT with OTA configuration for sensor thresholds. Local visual and audio alarms (LED and buzzer) are shown on a 16×2 I2C LCD, and the dashboard offers dark/light modes and 7‑day historical analytics. The hardware uses an ESP32 microcontroller, DHT22 sensor, Sharp GP2Y1010AU0F PM2.5 sensor, MQ‑Series gas sensor, and a 16×2 LCD. The project was presented at RMUTT on March 14 2026, and you can view it at https://airmonitorpro.netlify.app/ or explore the source code on GitHub at https://github.com/Automatic28m/air_monitor_iot.

variants.verbatim: What is the Thaivel tourism website project and what are its main features and technologies?
variants.partial: What Thaivel tourism website project are
variants.natural: the Thaivel tourism website project and what are its main features and technologies?

items.reference_answer: Thaivel is a sophisticated full‑stack travel platform created as a showcase for the International Web Design Contest (iWDC). It serves as a curated gateway to Thailand’s attractions, organizing destinations by the country’s six regions and allowing users to filter by categories such as cafes, nature spots, restaurants, street food, temples and urban sites. Key features include a regional exploration guide, a smart categorization engine, the “Tuktuk Driver AI” conversational travel assistant, dark‑themed interactive maps with custom pins, a mobile‑first responsive design, and social‑media and Google Maps integration for each location. The site was built with Next.js (React) on the front end, styled with Tailwind CSS, and uses MySQL for the destination database. It was presented at RMUTT on 7 April 2026 and the source code is available at https://github.com/Automatic28m/thaivel.
